topStories.headline: 'The Chosen' Wraps Its Final Season at Midlothian's Camp Hoblitzelle
topStories.dek: After nearly five months of filming, the biblical drama's seventh and last season has finished production at the Ellis County campus that has been its home since Season 3.
topStories.body:
Cameras stopped rolling this week on the seventh and final season of "The Chosen" in Midlothian, capping a nearly five-month shoot at Camp Hoblitzelle that began in late April. The biblical drama about the life of Jesus has primarily filmed at the Salvation Army's more-than-1,200-acre campus since Season 3, where the production built 150,000 square feet of studio space and sets — including a full-scale replica of the ancient fishing village of Capernaum that hosted more than 500 days of filming across the run of the series.

To mark the end of production, local press were invited to tour the set on September 21. Creator and director Dallas Jenkins spoke to reporters and expressed hope that the Midlothian facilities would continue to be used on future projects. "I do hope that on other projects, we have a chance to use some of these facilities and this great landscape and the great people that we have here," Jenkins told the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. Jenkins's production company, 5&2 Studios, is based in Midlothian and will continue producing additional biblical content beyond the flagship series.

Season 7, which will depict the Resurrection, filmed across a Texas summer that production designer James Cunningham described as authentically challenging but consistent for outdoor work. The show — which started as a crowdfunded effort and grew into a worldwide audience of more than 300 million viewers — struck a streaming deal with Amazon Prime Video in 2025, and over $70 million was raised for Season 7 alone, according to a show spokesperson.

Season 6, covering the Crucifixion, is scheduled to air in November. Midlothian's Camp Hoblitzelle was chosen in part because the Texas landscape bears some resemblance to the biblical Galilee, and the production used Pompeii as a reference point for set details, even copying graffiti found in Pompeii onto the walls of the show's Roman quarter.

topStories.headline: I-35E Closes Through Red Oak Corridor; Detours Expected Through Late 2026
topStories.dek: A long-term TxDOT rebuild project has shut down all northbound lanes between FM 664/Ovilla Road and Bear Creek Road, with signed detours now in place.
topStories.body:
Red Oak commuters are facing a major disruption on I-35E after the Texas Department of Transportation closed all northbound lanes between FM 664/Ovilla Road and Bear Creek Road beginning the night of Wednesday, September 24. The first closures started Tuesday, September 23, and the northbound lanes between those two points will remain detoured through late 2026 as part of an ongoing large-scale corridor improvement project.

Work associated with the rebuild includes demolishing portions of the Ovilla Road overpass, rebuilding pavement and bridges, and realigning lanes to increase capacity and safety along the Red Oak corridor. Signed detours are in place, but Red Oak city officials are advising motorists to allow extra travel time, watch for posted signage, and check DriveTexas.org for updates on nightly work schedules.

Traffic will funnel onto frontage roads and alternate routes during peak hours. Local businesses along the corridor say they anticipate shifts in customer traffic patterns as commuters seek alternative routes. While the project is expected to bring long-term safety and capacity benefits to the fast-growing area, officials acknowledge the short-term impact will be significant for residents in Red Oak, Ovilla, and surrounding communities.

topStories.headline: Midlothian Adopts FY 2026-27 Budget and Tax Rate of $0.64 per $100
topStories.dek: The city ratified a new tax rate at a special called meeting on September 9, setting spending priorities for the coming fiscal year as the city's automated trash program also takes hold.
topStories.body:
The City of Midlothian formally adopted its fiscal year 2026-2027 budget and tax rate at a special called meeting on September 9, 2026. The adopted rate is $0.64 per $100 of assessed value — split between $0.336585 for maintenance and operations and $0.303415 for interest and sinking — and is projected to generate approximately $28.6 million for operations and $25.8 million for debt service, calculated at a 99 percent collection assumption.

City finance staff opened public hearings on the proposed budget and rate at the August 25 council meeting. No members of the public signed up to speak on the city operating budget at that session. The city posted required taxpayer impact statements and advertised the hearings in accordance with the Texas Local Government Code.

The adopted budget coincides with a busy period of municipal change. Midlothian launched a new automated residential trash and recycling program on August 3 under a five-year contract with Waste Connections, replacing the previous system with 95-gallon standardized black carts for trash and blue carts for recycling at all residential properties. The city council had approved the Waste Connections contract 6-1 in April. Trash is now collected twice weekly and recycling every other Wednesday for most residents.

events.title: Ovilla Annual Heritage Day Celebration
events.location: Park grounds behind Ovilla City Hall, 105 S. Cockrell Hill Rd, Ovilla
events.description: Ovilla's annual Heritage Day celebration — held each year on the last Saturday of September — kicks off with a parade from Ovilla Road Baptist Church, followed by live entertainment, vendors, food trucks, a car show, petting zoo, and bounce houses. The 2025 edition was the 40th anniversary.

events.title: Chamber Bingo: Island Nights
events.description: The Midlothian Chamber of Commerce's annual signature fundraiser features a tropical-themed evening of bingo, exciting prizes, music, raffles, and costumes. Proceeds support the Chamber's mission to strengthen local businesses and the community.

events.title: Red Oak Fall Festival
events.location: Pearson Park & Red Oak Municipal Center, 200 Lakeview Pkwy, Red Oak
events.description: The City of Red Oak's free family festival includes live entertainment, face painting, glitter tattoos, a petting zoo, pony rides, a trackless train, inflatables, fall crafts, and candy. Presented by the City of Red Oak and Compass Datacenters; admission and all activities are free.

events.title: Midlothian Annual Scarecrow Festival
events.description: The Midlothian Downtown Business Association presents its annual Scarecrow Festival with this year's theme of movies. Scarecrow entry forms are due October 10, installation runs October 10–16, and all displays must be removed by November 3.

events.title: Battle Axes Axe Throwing League — Season 4
events.location: Battle Axes, 1704 W FM 875, Bldg A, Ste 100, Midlothian
events.description: Ellis County's affiliated axe and knife throwing venue launches its Season 4 competitive league on October 5, running through December 13, 2026. Open to all skill levels with league registration available at the venue.

moreNews.headline: Ellis County Burn Ban Remains in Effect Across Unincorporated Areas
moreNews.body: The Ellis County Commissioners' Court voted to impose a county-wide burn ban at its meeting on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. The ban took effect immediately and as of this week remains active, covering all unincorporated areas of Ellis County — including rural portions of the Midlothian, Red Oak, and Ovilla areas. Residents should check the county's official burn ban page at elliscountytx.gov before any outdoor burning.

moreNews.headline: Voter Registration Deadline for November 3 Election Is October 5
moreNews.body: Ellis County residents have until Monday, October 5, 2026, to register to vote or update their voter registration records to participate in the November 3, 2026, General and Special Elections. Early voting runs October 19–30. The Ellis County Elections Office is located at 204 E. Jefferson Street, Waxahachie; residents can also register through the Texas Secretary of State's website.
